finding.claim: Authorization bypass: any authenticated user can invoke the DROP TABLE path in dropTable because the Authorize result is discarded.
finding.source: Authenticated HTTP request to /admin/drop from a user with any role (user loaded from request context).
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27, a destructive DBA-only operation.

trace.note: User is loaded from request context via userFrom.
Authorize(u, "dba") is called but its error return is discarded.
DROP statement executes regardless of the authorization result.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct in isolation but its result is ignored. No early return, no if err != nil, no other role check. vacuum (api.go:33-36) performs the same check correctly, so the defect is specific to dropTable.

verdict.guard_found: none. Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and never tests the result. The only other check is in vacuum (api.go:33-36), which is a different handler. Nothing else between the route (api.go:44) and runSQL (api.go:27) blocks the request. runSQL receives a raw string concatenation of r.FormValue("t") with no allowlist or parameterization.
verdict.reason: The route at api.go:44 reaches dropTable, which discards the Authorize error at api.go:26 and runs the DROP at api.go:27, so any authenticated user with a non-dba role can drop tables.

finding.claim: SQL injection: the table name from the request is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement without validation.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or form body, fully attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: runSQL at api.go:27 with string concatenation.

trace.note: t is read via r.FormValue and concatenated into the SQL text.
The resulting string is passed to runSQL without parameterization or identifier quoting.

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist of table names, no identifier quoting, no input validation, no parameterization. runSQL is a stub (api.go:41), so stacked-statement behaviour depends on the real driver and is unverified. Reachable by any authenticated user via F1.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is the only control. It returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement, so it does not block the request. No table-name allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameterization exists between r.FormValue("t") (api.go:27) and runSQL. The userFrom call at api.go:25 requires a user in the request context, which is the only gate, so the attacker must be authenticated but need not hold the dba role.
verdict.reason: api.go:27 concatenates the attacker-controlled "t" form value into "DROP TABLE " with no validation, and the role check at api.go:26 discards Authorize's error, so any authenticated user can reach it. runSQL at api.go:41 is a stub, so the actual driver behaviour is unverified, but the flaw is present in the code as written.

finding.claim: Possible missing authentication: admin routes are registered with no auth middleware visible in this file, and userFrom performs an unchecked type assertion.
finding.sink: Unchecked assertion r.Context().Value("user").(*User) at api.go:22, and Authorize(u, ...) dereferencing u.Roles at api.go:14 on a possibly nil user.

trace.note: Handlers are registered directly on http.DefaultServeMux with no auth wrapper.
If no middleware set the "user" context value, the type assertion panics. net/http recovers per request, so the impact is request-level.
Server listens on :8083 on all interfaces with no TLS.

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no nil check on the user, no typed context key, and no TLS within this file. Middleware may exist outside this directory; not verified. Candidate only, pending review of the surrounding service.

verdict.guard_found: Within the codebase, the only file is api.go and nothing sets the "user" context value. userFrom's unchecked assertion at api.go:22 (called at api.go:25 and :32) panics on every request before any effect, so runSQL at api.go:27 is never reached. For /admin/vacuum, Authorize at api.go:33-35 is checked and effective. For /admin/drop, Authorize at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error is discarded, so it is not a guard, but the panic at api.go:25 blocks the path first.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate, but no request can reach the effect: userFrom at api.go:22 panics at api.go:25 before runSQL at api.go:27, and nothing in the codebase sets the "user" context value, so an anonymous request does nothing. The candidate also misses a real latent bug: dropTable discards Authorize's result at api.go:26 and passes r.FormValue("t") straight into SQL at api.go:27. That would be a broken-access-control and SQL-injection issue for any authenticated non-dba user if a middleware outside this codebase set the user context, so it should be filed as a separate, conditional finding.

finding.claim: Possible CSRF on a destructive operation: dropTable uses r.FormValue, which accepts query-string parameters, and performs no method restriction or CSRF token check.
finding.source: A cross-site request to /admin/drop carrying the "t" parameter in the URL or form body, relying on ambient credentials.

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") accepts both GET query parameters and POST form fields.
The destructive statement executes without a method check or anti-forgery token.

finding.guards_checked: No method check, no CSRF token, no SameSite or Origin validation in this file. Depends on whether authentication is cookie-based, which is not visible here. Candidate only.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 has its error return discarded as a bare statement, so it does not block the call. No method check, CSRF token, or Origin/SameSite check exists in api.go:24-29. The auth middleware that sets the "user" context value (api.go:22) is not in this directory.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 accepts query and form values, and the statement runs unguarded), and no CSRF guard exists in api.go:24-29, but whether a cross-site request carries credentials depends on cookie-based auth in middleware not present here, so the CSRF claim cannot be decided from this code. Separately, api.go:26 discards the Authorize error, so any request that reaches dropTable with a valid user (any role) can run DROP TABLE, a stronger authorization defect that the candidate does not describe.
